change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut (inverted condition and wrong offset)
findings.body: The token id is `<2 session><2 tokenType><2 grant>:<uuid>`, so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`. The code takes `substring(3, 5)`, which is the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant. It also returns `false` when that substring *equals* the expected shortcut. Because the offsets are wrong, the equality can never hold for a valid id, so the check never rejects anything. The matcher then accepts any `x:uuid` string with one colon. A regression where `expectCodeToToken` or `expectRefresh` produced the wrong grant, or `na`, would pass. If only the offset were fixed, every correct id would fail because of the inverted condition. Use `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` and check `items[0].length() == 6` first. `describeTo` should also say what is expected, for example "access token id with grant shortcut X and UUID".

findings.title: requireNonNull checks grantType twice, rawTokenId never checked
findings.body: Line 73 is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. It should check `rawTokenId`. A null raw id is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then produces an id ending in `:null`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not because of the validation
findings.body: `before()` never sets `factory.sessionFactory`, and `ac` is not in the test maps. `getGrantTypeByShortcut` therefore falls into its refresh branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` on null. That throws a NullPointerException, which `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows. The `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` path is never exercised. Mock the session factory to return no matching factory and catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically. The `getGrantTypeByShortcut` refresh branch and the duplicate-shortcut check in `postInit` have no tests either. Separately, every `assertEquals` in this file passes (actual, expected) in the wrong order, which gives misleading failure messages.

findings.title: Client-credentials (and UMA, legacy token exchange, implicit/hybrid) tokens never get a GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their ids encode as `na`
findings.body: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` reads `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` from the ClientSessionContext and falls back to `na`. The attribute is set only in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (auth code, CIBA, device), in ROPC, in `refreshAccessToken`, in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` and in `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType`. `ClientCredentialsGrantType` builds its token through `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` and never sets the attribute. A grep for `GRANT_TYPE` in that file finds nothing. The same applies to `AuthorizationTokenService` (UMA, shortcut `pg`) and `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` (legacy exchange). It also applies to tokens issued by `OIDCLoginProtocol`, which is the implicit/hybrid flow. The shortcut `cc` registered here is never used for real tokens. The unit test's `trltcc:` id is therefore never produced, because client-credentials tokens come out as `trltna:`. Set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` in `ClientCredentialsGrantType`, and likewise for the other grants that should be identifiable. If the omission is deliberate and meant for a follow-up, say so in the PR.

findings.title: grantType is cached in the constructor but setFormParams does not update it
findings.body: `grantType` is derived once from `formParams` in the constructor. The public `setFormParams` replaces `formParams` without refreshing `grantType`, so the two can diverge. `createTokenResponse` now relies on `getGrantType()` for the token id. Either recompute `grantType` in `setFormParams` or make `getGrantType()` read `formParams.getFirst(...)`. The constructor also now throws an NPE on null `formParams`, which it tolerated before. The only caller, `TokenEndpoint`, never passes null.

contracts.action: Every access token created via TokenManager.initToken now gets a jti of the form `<session><tokenType><grant>:<uuid>` instead of a bare UUID
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code was `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())`. Other jti/id generators, such as the refresh token id, are untouched.
contracts.before_after: Before: 36-char UUID. After: 43-char `xxyyzz:uuid`. The encoder reads the session state, `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` and the Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute. Unset attribute becomes `na`; transient, offline and online sessions are handled. encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException only for UNKNOWN session or token type, which cannot come from this path.
contracts.visible_effect: The `jti` claim in access tokens, `Details.TOKEN_ID` in events and the introspection `jti` change format. Anything that parses or validates the jti as a UUID is affected.
contracts.failure_mode: If the provider is missing, or a grant type's shortcut is not registered, token creation throws and the token request fails. Grant types that never set the attribute silently encode `na`.

contracts.action: OAuth2GrantType.Context now captures grant_type from the form params, and createTokenResponse writes it into the ClientSessionContext
contracts.equivalent_path: ROPC, refresh, standard token exchange and pre-authorized code set the attribute individually. Client credentials, UMA and legacy token exchange do not.
contracts.before_after: The attribute is set before createClientAccessToken, so initToken sees it. For `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType` the constant factory id is used. Nothing is set for client credentials.
contracts.visible_effect: The grant shortcut inside the jti is correct for the grants that set the attribute, and `na` for the rest.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent `na` for the grants that do not set it. A stale `grantType` is possible if setFormParams is used.

summary: The change adds a token-context encoder SPI and encodes session type, token type and grant shortcut into access-token jti values. The main problems are in the tests. `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` never checks the grant shortcut, because the condition is inverted and the substring offset is wrong. `testIncorrectGrantType` passes through an NPE rather than the validation it names. `AccessTokenContext` null-checks `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`. Client-credentials, UMA, legacy token exchange and implicit/hybrid tokens never set the grant attribute, so their ids encode as `na` even though shortcuts such as `cc` are registered. The new abstract `getShortcut()` on the SPI factory breaks third-party grant factories. The jti format change is visible to anything that treats the jti as a UUID. I did not build or run anything.
